title: SELLING A SERVICE
content:
A service is work performed for or with a customer. The thing being sold may be your expertise, labor, judgment, implementation, access, or a defined result.

Services can be local or remote, one-off or recurring, highly customized or standardized. That is why "service" is a delivery type rather than a complete business model by itself.

THE CENTRAL TRADEOFF IS OFTEN TIME
If every new customer requires another hour of your direct work, income can become closely tied to your available hours. That may be perfectly acceptable, especially when starting. It simply means capacity belongs in the decision.

Some services can later become less time-dependent through standardized packages, group delivery, delegation, automation, templates, systems, or other changes. That does not mean every service needs to become passive.

SERVICES CAN BE FAST TO START
If you already have a useful skill, a service may require less upfront product development or inventory than many other paths. The challenge is making the service specific enough that a customer understands what they are buying.

WHAT TO DECIDE NEXT
Do you already have a service idea, or do you need to discover what service you could sell?

I NEED TO FIGURE OUT WHAT SERVICE I COULD SELL → PDF 40.
I ALREADY HAVE A SERVICE IDEA → PDF 42.

EXAMPLES OF DIFFERENT SERVICE SHAPES

A bookkeeper may provide recurring monthly bookkeeping. A photographer may sell a one-time family photo session. A designer may sell a fixed website package. A consultant may work one-on-one on a custom engagement. A cleaner may provide weekly local service.

All are services, but the customer relationship, capacity, pricing structure, and repeat pattern differ.

WHERE TO GO NEXT
Continue to PDF 40 if you need to discover a service. Continue to PDF 42 if you already know what service you want to examine.
